steps.prompt: $|x|$ is the distance from $x$ to $0$. How many numbers are at distance $4$ from $0$? Which numbers are at distance $4$ from $7$?

cards.title: Absolute value is a distance
cards.body: $|a|$ is the distance from $a$ to $0$, so it is never negative. $|x - c|$ is the distance from $x$ to $c$. So $|x - c| = d$ has two solutions, $c + d$ and $c - d$, when $d > 0$; one when $d = 0$; and none when $d < 0$.

cards.title: Inequalities with absolute value
cards.body: $|x - c| < d$ means $x$ is within $d$ of $c$: $c - d < x < c + d$. $|x - c| > d$ means $x$ is further than $d$ away. To count the whole numbers from $a$ to $b$, both included, use $b - a + 1$.

steps.text: $|x + 2| = |x - (-2)|$ is the distance from $x$ to $-2$. So $-7 < x < 3$.
The ends don't count (strict $<$): the integers are $-6, -5, \ldots, 2$, and $2 - (-6) + 1 = 9$.

cards.title: The common trap: losing or inventing solutions
cards.body: $|x + 2|$ is the distance to $-2$, not to $2$. $|x| = -3$ has NO solutions. When the other side has $x$ in it, like $|x - 4| = 2x - 5$, check each answer in the original: some cases give fake solutions. And with $<$ the ends don't count.

prompts: How does thinking of $|x - c|$ as a distance help you solve problems faster?
